title: Bookkeeping, payroll and online booking for Pakistan’s barbershops
role: Mobile app, API and web admin
summary: Trimmo replaces the notebook with one app for daily earnings, worker pay and customer bookings. Built in about 12 weeks and now live on Google Play as Barber Hub.

children.value: The problem

A typical Pakistani barbershop runs on cash and memory. At closing time the owner needs three answers: how much did we earn today (aaj ki kamai), how much did we spend (kharcha), and how much do I owe each worker (kitne dene hain). The third one is the hard one.

Shops pay workers in different ways, sometimes several in the same shop: a straight commission split like 30/70, a cut off the top for chair, power and products and then a split, a fixed monthly salary, and advances (udhaar) taken mid-month that must come off what the worker is owed. Owners keep all of this in a notebook or in their heads, and the result is disputes, revenue that never gets written down, and no idea whether the shop actually makes a profit.

Customers have the mirror problem. They walk in and wait, shops have no simple way to take bookings without a receptionist, and nobody can find a nearby shop with a free slot. General salon apps didn’t fit: they are priced in dollars, built around card payments, English only, and blind to how local shops actually pay their workers.
The approach

We designed around one closing-time screen and the people who use it. A worker logs a haircut in a few taps, the owner approves it, and the split is worked out and saved at that moment, so changing a worker’s commission later never rewrites past earnings. Labels use the words owners already say (Kamai, Kharcha, Hisaab), money is entered on big number pads, and workers sign in with a shop code, phone number and 4-digit PIN, no email needed.
Owners, workers and customers each get their own simple view of the app, so nobody has to wade through screens that aren’t meant for them.
The solution
Shop operations

The Today screen shows revenue, expenses, what the shop keeps, who is clocked in, what is waiting for approval and what each worker is still owed. Workers log jobs and expenses, and owners approve or reject them, with undo, and any price changed by hand is flagged. Hisaab brings jobs, expenses and payments into one ledger, a pay ledger tracks settlements and advances so the balance is always clear, and a monthly statement can be downloaded as a PDF.
Pay that matches the chair

Every shop’s pay arrangement is handled. On a Rs 300 haircut, a 30/70 commission gives Rs 90 to the shop and Rs 210 to the worker. A 10% shop cut then 30/70 gives Rs 30 to the shop upfront, then Rs 81 to the shop and Rs 189 to the worker. On monthly salary, the Rs 300 stays with the shop and the salary appears on the monthly statement. Every change to an approved entry is recorded, so there is always a clear trail when a question comes up.
Online booking for customers

Customers find nearby shops in a list or on a map, pick their services, choose a barber or “Any barber”, and see only the time slots that are really free, based on shop hours, days off and breaks. They get a reminder 15 minutes before the appointment, and a completed booking is added to the shop’s books automatically, so online and walk-in revenue sit in one place.
The rule is simple: a booking reserves a chair, and walk-ins fill the gaps. Booking a specific barber is confirmed straight away, while “Any barber” bookings wait for the owner to assign someone.
Branches and managers

Owners with more than one shop get an all-branches overview with combined revenue, a card for each branch, and the option to put a manager in charge of each one. Single shops carry on exactly as before.
Plans for every shop

Trimmo is free to start, with paid plans for busier shops and for businesses with several branches. Upgrades are arranged locally through JazzCash, Easypaisa or bank transfer, so owners never need a card. Even on the free plan, owners can always record expenses and workers can always clock in.
The result

In about 12 weeks, from the first line of work on 4 September to multi-branch support on 23 November 2026, Trimmo went from an idea to a live product on Google Play. Owners get a clear answer at closing time, workers know exactly what they are owed, and customers can book a chair without a phone call.
Trimmo is live on Google Play under the name Barber Hub.
